newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips claw back losses, close firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips claw back losses, close firm.

text.p: Argentine leading stocks soaked up profit-taking and advanced in their sixth consecutive gain at the close Friday, dealers said.

"The market paused today and the international market scenario favored profit-taking," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro. "But players saw the drop as a buying opportunity and increased their exposure selectively."

The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV recovered from a low of 719.58 and closed up 0.1 percent at 725.49, with a weekly gain of 3.2 percent. The broad market, however, snapped its winning streak and shed 0.6 percent.
Losers edged out winners 30 to 26 and 16 issues closed flat.

"The market capped a powerful week and we could see less activity in the next few days, especially Monday with the Wall Street holiday. But the MerVal is poised to knock down resistance at 730," another trader said.
The MerVal topped out at 728 in February 1994. If it reaches that level again it would stand at a five-year high.
Floor volume remained strong at 36.9 million pesos Friday, compared to 36 millon Thursday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 101.2 million pesos from 168 million Thursday.
Best main-tier performers were electricity companies Central Costanera and Central Puerto, which rallied 5.4 percent and 3.2 perdent, respectively, and carmaker Sevel, up 2.0 pecent.
MerVal losers were led by oil company Astra and Bansud Bank, off 2.6 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively, and Telecom and holding company Comercial del Plata, both down 2.0 percent.
